root_cause.text: The goldfish battery driver registers the IRQ handler using devm_request_irq before registering the power supply device with devm_power_supply_register, causing the power supply to be freed before the IRQ handler is unregistered during device removal, leading to a use-after-free in power_supply_changed() when an interrupt fires after the power supply is freed but before the IRQ is released.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the devm_request_irq call after the devm_power_supply_register calls, and the commit message states: "Using the `devm_` variant for requesting IRQ _before_ the `devm_` variant for allocating/registering the `power_supply` handle, means that the `power_supply` handle will be deallocated/unregistered _before_ the interrupt handler ... resulting in a race condition where an interrupt can fire just _after_ the `power_supply` handle has been freed."

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch moves the devm_request_irq call after the devm_power_supply_register calls, and the commit message states: "Using the `devm_` variant for requesting IRQ _before_ the `devm_` variant for allocating/registering the `power_supply` handle, means that the `power_supply` handle will be deallocated/unregistered _before_ the interrupt handler ... resulting in a race condition where an interrupt can fire just _after_ the `power_supply` handle has been freed."

candidates.rationale: This check ensures an IRQ exists before proceeding, but it does not prevent the ordering issue; the IRQ handler is still registered too early relative to the power supply.
This registers the IRQ handler using devm_* before the power supply device is registered, causing the handler to remain active after the power supply is freed during removal (use-after-free).
This specifies the interrupt handler that will later call power_supply_changed() on a freed power supply because it is registered before the supply is created.
This completes the IRQ request with the shared flag and driver data; the data pointer is used in the handler and becomes stale after power supply is freed.

This assigns the driver data to the power supply configuration, but the IRQ handler can access the same data before or after the supply is registered, contributing to the use-after-free if the supply is freed first.

This registers the AC power supply device after the IRQ handler is already registered; during remove, the power supply is freed before the IRQ is unregistered due to devres order, leading to use-after-free in the IRQ handler.

This specifies the interrupt handler that will later call power_supply_changed() on a freed power supply because it is registered before the supply is created, leading to use-after-free.
This completes the IRQ request with the shared flag and driver data; the 'data' pointer becomes stale after the power supply is freed, causing use-after-free when the handler accesses it.

This registers the AC power supply device using devm_* after the IRQ handler is already registered. During device removal, devres frees the power supply before unregistering the IRQ handler, enabling the use-after-free.

This condition guards the IRQ registration; while not directly causing the use-after-free, it is part of the code path that registers the IRQ handler too early, contributing to the vulnerable ordering.
This assigns driver data to the power supply configuration; the IRQ handler can access the same data, and the stale pointer after the power supply is freed is part of the use-after-free chain.
